newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply lower, funds sell.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply lower, funds sell.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended sharply lower Tuesday on moderate volume after the rally in complex of the past month ran out of momentum, traders said.

"The whole complex got overextended and the charts look pretty ugly, with short term trend line support breaking in gold today, prompting some fund selling," Credit Lyonnais Rouse chief bullion dealer Scott Mehlman said.
"The other factor was the renewed strength of the dollar, with the German economy still looking weak," he said.
COMEX April gold ended down $3.30 at $360.40 an ounce, traded $364.50 to $360.10.
Estimated volume was 43,000 contracts.
In the bullion market, spot gold closed quoted at $358.60/$359.10 against the London afternoon fix of $359.40 and the New York close Monday of $361.70/$362.20.

COMEX gold open interest rose for the second day in a row Monday, in data released Tuesday, suggesting funds could be going short again, now gold's rally looks to have run into resistance near $370.00 an ounce, analysts noted.
COMEX gold open interest was up 1,239 lots Monday at 179,281, after rising 4,783 lots Friday. Earlier open interest fell more than 23,000 lots as funds covered short positions in the past two weeks.

But COMEX April gold reached overbought levels on both a standard five-day stochastic and nine-day RSI (relative strength indicator) last week, so a correction this week was not a surprise, traders said.
But the recovery in the past month from three year lows around $336.00 still looked intact, analysts said.
The Dutch central bank data for the week ending March 3 confirmed the sale of 300 tonnes of gold, announced in mid-January, had been at least partially settled in February.
COMEX May silver closed down 7.5 cents at $5.265 after trading from $5.35 to $5.25.
The momentum of the rally in silver since mid-January is also waning though, analysts said, with momentum oscillators drifting back toward neutral positions.
NYMEX April platinum lost $2.50 to close at $389.50 after breaching short term support around $390 and breaching the lows of the past two days.
April platinum also became overbought last week, and failed to close the week above $400, after a spike up to a seven month high at $415.00 intraday Friday.
NYMEX June palladium ended down $4.80 an ounce at $151.50.
But fundamental factors remain supportive for the platinum group metals, analysts said, with uncertainties continuing about Russian supplies.
"If worries over Russian supplies persist, (palladium) prices could be pushed toward resistance at $160," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.
Workers at Russia's Norilsk plant gave management a 10-day deadline to meet wage arrears demand Monday and threatened to strike.
The Norilsk mine produces almost all of Russia's platinum and palladium as by-products to its nickel output.
No shipments of palladium are expected to Japan in March either, following the breakdown of the Russia/Japan supply contract talks last December.
Russia is the world's main supplier of palladium and the second largest supplier of platinum, while Japan is the world's largest consumer of both metals.
